title: Tiger Fitness: Firefighter CPAT Training
author: Mithosphere
desc:
INTRODUCTION
The CPAT is not a fitness test you can talk your way through. It is a timed sequence of loaded work performed in a weighted vest. This is a 10-week, 4-day program built to prepare an intermediate trainee for that kind of work: climbing stairs under load, dragging, carrying, pulling hand over hand, swinging and crawling, in the durations that actually show up on the clock. You do not need a barbell for any of it. You need a sled, dumbbells, kettlebells, a stair machine or a real stairwell, and a vest.

WHO IS THIS PROGRAM FOR
- Candidates with a Candidate Physical Ability Test date on the calendar in roughly three months, who already train and can handle four hard sessions a week.
- Lifters who are strong in the gym but gas out the moment the work becomes continuous and loaded.
- Anyone training in a facility with a sled, dumbbells, kettlebells and a stair machine but no barbell, rack or bench.
- Current firefighters and academy recruits who want a structured off-season block for stair, drag and carry capacity.

Who this is NOT for: beginners. If you cannot yet do 20 clean push ups, hold a 60 second plank and walk 100 feet with a heavy dumbbell in each hand without setting them down, spend eight weeks building a base first.

HOW TO PROGRESS
Four blocks across the ten weeks, and the vest is the main dial you turn.
WEEKS 1-3
Use a vest weight you can carry for three unbroken minutes of stairs without grabbing the rails, and a sled load that lets you finish all five rounds at the same speed.
WEEKS 4-6
Add load. Put 5 to 10 pounds on the vest, and add weight to the sled on Day 3 rather than adding rounds. The stair times stay where they are; the vest is what changes. Day 4 keeps its three 5 minute rounds, and you should be finishing the third one at the same step rate as the first.
WEEK 7 - DELOAD
Cut every working exercise to two sets on Day 1 and Day 2. On Day 3 and Day 4, cut every movement to two rounds. Drop the vest back to your week 1 weight and keep the sled light enough that nothing burns.
WEEKS 8-10
Rehearse. Vest at the load your department specifies for the stair event. Shorten the recoveries on Day 3 and Day 4 by 10 seconds each week, and never take any recovery below 30 seconds, so the carries and drags start to run together the way they do on the clock without a row ending up with no rest at all. Leave the loads and the distances alone in these three weeks; the only variable moving is rest. In the last week before your test, train Day 1 and Day 2 only, at half the volume, and let the rest go.

WARM-UP & RECOVERY
5 minutes easy on the stair machine or a slow walk, then Worlds Greatest Stretch for 5 slow reps a side, Hip Flexor Stretch for 30 seconds a side, Cat Cow Stretch for 10 reps, and one light set of the first movement of the day. On Day 3 and 4, add one unloaded trip up and back with the empty sled before the first working round. Do not skip the shoulder prep on Day 2.
